facts.statement: The genus Nullotitan honors paleontologist Francisco Nullo and is a lithostrotian titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina.
facts.quote: Nullotitan (meaning "Nullo's giant", in honor of paleontologist Francisco Nullo) is an extinct genus of lithostrotian titanosaur dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Geologist Francisco E. Nullo first noticed sauropod bones at the Estancia Alta Vista site in 1980.
facts.quote: In 1980, geologist Francisco E. Nullo noticed the presence of sauropod bones on a hillside of the Estancia Alta Vista, south of the Centinela River in the Santa Cruz province of Argentina.

facts.statement: The species Nullotitan glaciaris was formally named and described by Fernando Emilio Novas and colleagues in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species Nullotitan glaciaris was named and described by Fernando Emilio Novas and colleagues.

facts.statement: The species name glaciaris refers to the Perito Moreno Glacier visible near the fossil discovery site.
facts.quote: The specific name, glaciaris, refers to the Perito Moreno Glacier, visible from the discovery site.

facts.statement: The holotype fossils date to the Campanian–Maastrichtian stages of the lower Chorrillo Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MACN-PV 18644 and MPM 21542, was found in a layer of the lower Chorrillo Formation that dates from the Campanian–Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including a cervical vertebra found in 1981, tail vertebrae, ribs, a scapula, and leg bones.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton without a skull, comprising a third cervical vertebra (the MACN-PV 18644 specimen found by Bonaparte in 1981), caudal vertebrae, a cervical rib, dorsal ribs, a left scapula, the ends of a right femur, and a right tibia, fibula, and astragalus.

facts.statement: The holotype individual of Nullotitan was more than 20 meters long.
facts.quote: Nullotitan is a large sauropod. The holotype specimen belongs to an animal more than 20 m in length.

facts.statement: Nullotitan falls into a "medium body size" category for sauropods, which includes animals between 12 and 22 meters long.
facts.quote: This places Nullotitan in the "medium body size" class of González Riga et al. (2022), comprising sauropods with an estimated body length between 12 - 22 m.

facts.statement: The front and middle tail vertebrae feature large depressions on their sides and undersides.
facts.quote: The anterior and middle caudal vertebrae are laterally and ventrally excavated by large depressions.

facts.statement: The fibula exhibits a distinct S-shaped curve when viewed from the front or back.
facts.quote: Viewed from the front or back, the fibula has a notable sigmoid curvature.

facts.statement: The front tail vertebrae have centra that are twice as wide as they are long.
facts.quote: The vertebral centra of the anterior caudal vertebrae are remarkably short, twice as wide as long.

facts.statement: Middle tail vertebrae possess a large pit on the side below the transverse process.
facts.quote: The middle caudal vertebrae have a large fossa on the side below the transverse process.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Nullotitan lack internal air pockets (pneumatization).
facts.quote: The tail vertebrae lack pneumatization.

facts.statement: Middle tail vertebrae have a deep groove running lengthwise on the underside between two thick ridges.
facts.quote: The middle caual vertebrae have a deep longitudinal furrow on the underside between two thick ridges.

facts.statement: The bottom of the tibia is flattened front-to-back and wider across than in other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The lower end of the tibia is flattened from the front to the rear and widened more across than in other titanosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype's neck vertebra is 45 cm long and 22 cm high, excluding the broken arch.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebra of the holotype is elongated with a length of 45 cm and rather low with a height of 22 cm, apart from the broken neural arch.

facts.statement: The neck vertebra contains many small internal air chambers called camellae.
facts.quote: The bone has many small air chambers internally, known as camellae.

facts.statement: The first tail vertebra measures approximately 25 cm in length and 40 cm in width.
facts.quote: The first caudal vertebra is approximately 25 cm long and 40 cm wide.

facts.statement: A referred humerus is 114 cm long and has a robustness index of 0.28.
facts.quote: The humerus of MPM 21545 is 114 cm long. It is relatively slim, with a robustness index (RI) of 0.28.

facts.statement: The holotype tibia is 105 cm long and is robust with a very wide lower end.
facts.quote: The tibia of the holotype is 105 cm long. It is robust and very wide at the bottom.

facts.statement: The fibula is 109 cm long, robust, and has a shaft that curves outward.
facts.quote: The fibula is 109 cm long. It is robust with an RI of 0.4 and a shaft that bows outwards.

facts.statement: Novas and colleagues initially classified Nullotitan as a colossosaurian titanosaur in 2019 without a phylogenetic test.
facts.quote: Novas et al. (2019) identified Nullotitan as a colossosaurian titanosaur in 2019. However, they did not perform a phylogenetic analysis to test these affinities.

facts.statement: Later analyses recovered Nullotitan as a lithostrotian titanosaur outside the group Colossosauria.
facts.quote: In both versions of the analysis, Nullotitan was recovered as a lithostrotian titanosaur, outside of the Colossosauria.

facts.statement: Nullotitan lived alongside the ornithopod dinosaur Isasicursor.
facts.quote: It was a contemporary of the ornithopod Isasicursor, which was described in the same paper.

facts.statement: The same formation contains fossils of the theropod Maip and the birds Kookne and Yatenavis.
facts.quote: Other named dinosaurs known from the formation include the elasmarian ornithopod Isasicursor, the megaraptorid theropod Maip, and the birds Kookne and Yatenavis.

facts.statement: Excavations revealed a new fauna across 2,000 square kilometers containing six bone concentrations linked to the original discovery.
facts.quote: A new fauna came to light in an area of 2000 km2, including six concentrations of bones that could be assigned to the original find, which was now recognized as a new sauropod species.

facts.statement: Titanosaur eggshells and sauropod teeth have been found in the same geological formation.
facts.quote: Titanosaur eggshells and sauropod teeth have also been found in the formation.

facts.statement: The holotype of Nullotitan represents an animal over 20 meters long and weighing 20 tons.
facts.quote: Los restos encontrados del holotipo son de un animal de más de 20 metros de longitud, 20 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: The anterior and middle tail vertebrae have sides and lower parts eroded by numerous large depressions that do not penetrate the bone wall.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola anterior y media tienen lados y partes inferiores erosionadas por numerosas depresiones grandes que no perforan la pared ósea.

facts.statement: Viewed from the front or back, the fibula has a notable wavy curve.
facts.quote: Desde la parte delantera o trasera, el peroné tiene una curva ondulante notable.

facts.statement: The humerus of specimen MPM 21545 is 114 centimeters long.
facts.quote: El húmero de MPM 21545 tiene 114 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The femur has lower articular nodules that are approximately the same size.
facts.quote: El fémur tiene nódulos articulares inferiores que son aproximadamente del mismo tamaño.

facts.statement: The tibia of the holotype measures 105 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: La tibia del holotipo tiene una longitud de 105 centímetros.

facts.statement: The fibula measures 109 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El peroné mide 109 centímetros.

facts.statement: Remains of Nullotitan were found in the Chorrillo Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en la Formación Chorrillo de la provincia de Santa Cruz en Argentina.

facts.statement: In 1980, geologist Francisco E. Nullo noted saurópod bones on a slope at Estancia Alta Vista, south of the Río Centinela in Santa Cruz Province.
facts.quote: En 1980, el geólogo Francisco E. Nullo notó la presencia de huesos de saurópodos en una ladera de la Estancia Alta Vista, al sur del Río Centinela en la provincia argentina de Santa Cruz.

facts.statement: José Bonaparte excavated a large cervical vertebra in 1981 and reported it as cf. Antarctosaurus.
facts.quote: Bonaparte desenterró una gran vértebra cervical en 1981 y lo reportó como un cf. Antarctosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Nullo and links it to a "Greek titan," referring to the great race of powerful giants from Greek mythology.
facts.quote: El nombre del género honra a Nullo y vincula su nombre a un "titán griego", refiriéndose a la gran raza de gigantes poderosos, los Titanes de la mitología griega.

facts.statement: The species name refers to the Perito Moreno Glacier, which is visible from the fossil site.
facts.quote: La designación de la especie se refiere al Glaciar Perito Moreno que es visible desde el sitio.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in a lower layer of the Chorrillo Formation dating to the Campanian-Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MACN-PV 18644; MPM 21542, fue encontrado en una capa inferior de la Formación Chorillo que data del Campaniense-Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton without a skull.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial sin cráneo.

facts.statement: Specimen MPM 21545 is a fragmentary skeleton consisting only of a humerus, a rib, and a vertebra.
facts.quote: MPM 21545 es un esqueleto fragmentario del cual solamente consisten un húmero, una costilla y una vértebra.

facts.statement: In 2019, Nullotitan was placed within Titanosauria in Colossosauria, though its precise relationships remain unclear.
facts.quote: Nullotitan se colocó dentro de Titanosauria en Colossosauria en 2019, aunque sus relaciones precisas aún no están claras.

facts.statement: The parent group of Nullotitan is Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lithostrotia

facts.statement: Nullotitan belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Nullotitan lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that epaxial tendons may have been anchored to the tail, holding it upward.
facts.quote: Quizás había tendones epaxiales anclados en él, sosteniendo la cola hacia arriba.

facts.statement: The large retractor muscle Musculus caudofemoralis, which pushed the femur backward, extended to the sixteenth vertebra.
facts.quote: El Musculus caudofemoralis, el gran músculo retractor que empujó el fémur hacia atrás, continuó hasta la decimosexta vértebra.

facts.statement: It is currently unknown whether the newly discovered series of five middle tail vertebrae at a different location have been excavated.
facts.quote: Estos aún no han sido excavados.
